html:
Vallabhbhai Patel was the organiser of the Indian National Congress and the first deputy prime minister of India. He joined more than 500 princely states to the new country. He is called Sardar, "chief", and the Iron Man of India.

He was a farmer's son from Gujarat who taught himself law, saved for years and qualified as a barrister in London at thirty-six. He met Gandhi in 1917 and gave up his practice and his European clothes. In 1928 he led the farmers of Bardoli in refusing a tax increase until the government backed down. He then ran the Congress machine for twenty years: he raised the money, chose the candidates and kept discipline.

In 1946 most provincial committees wanted him to lead Congress, and so the first government. Gandhi asked him to stand aside for Nehru, and he did.

As home minister from 1947 he dealt with the refugees of Partition and with the princes (see the integration of the princely states). He also kept the civil service on, as an all-India service.

He died in December 1950. A statue of him in Gujarat, finished in 2018, stands 182 metres high and is the tallest in the world.
